note: Frame decoding consumes a UTF-8-encoded frame/sample number from attacker-controlled input.
The UTF-8 parser repeatedly requests 8-bit chunks from the raw bitreader, so malformed continuation sequences drive it through the same internal buffer machinery.
Continuation bytes are accumulated into the decoded number, extending the parsing loop until the end of the malformed sequence.
Each 8-bit fetch indexes the current buffer word directly; if the stream is truncated, the cursor advances toward the tail of the buffer.
At a whole-word boundary the helper returns the current word without additional bounds checking, which is the key memory-safety sink for malformed bitstreams.
